name: chain-draws
title: Draws that remember
idea: Successive MCMC draws are usually positively correlated, so a pair probability estimated from them carries more Monte Carlo error than the iid formula says, and an iid error bound can fail far more often than its α.
from: new concept · theory book ch. 15 (dependent Monte Carlo; the two-state chain); postrank vignette m6 (loss traces, MCMC diagnostics) and pr_toy_mcmc; picture: a two-state trace with its running estimate and, under it, the spread of the estimate over many chains against the iid reference, the iid ±2 MCSE band and radius; the reader sets the stay probability, S and the number of chains
credit: After the postrank theory book, ch. 15, and the postrank vignette m6.
caption: Two units, one criterion: the posterior gives A above B and A below B one half each, after the postrank theory book, chapter 15; a posterior set by hand for teaching; postrank does not fit it. Every chain's first draw is A above B or A below B with chance one half each; the chains are simulated in this browser.
